clue.text: Drink fortified wine for comfort

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is a wine strengthened with brandy

explanation.surface: Someone reaches for a glass of port to console themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like a noun paired with the wine, but it is a verb giving a short word for sipping.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone in trouble is to give them emotional backing, the same sense as the noun and verb for helping someone through.

clue.text: Rare small vehicle by church

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a car is a vehicle
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rare little car is parked next to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, for Church of England, is the usual crossword abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is hard to find or in short supply, which is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Youngster accepting help having fulfilled financial obligations

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: a pup is a young animal, or informally a cheeky youth
aid means help

explanation.surface: A young person takes financial help and so clears their debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-letter young animal opens up to hold the three-letter word for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid-up member has settled every subscription or fee owed, so they have no outstanding debts.

clue.text: Generous and candid meeting worker and editor

indicators.note: things that are meeting join up side by side, so the parts are placed next to each other

blocks.note: a candid person is open and frank
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A kind, frank person is introduced to a labourer and an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'and' is only a link; 'Generous' alone is the definition, and 'candid' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed gives freely and without holding back, so the phrase describes a liberal, giving nature.

clue.text: Watch, say, brief getting upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: a remit is a brief, the scope of a task someone has been given

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on a friend who is briefly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective meaning short, but it is the noun for a set of instructions. 'Say' marks the watch as only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a device that measures and keeps track of elapsed time.

clue.text: Attacked appeal Victor developed

blocks.note: SA is sex appeal
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something that has developed over time has aged or matured

explanation.surface: A lawyer's appeal on behalf of someone called Victor was developed and then torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: SA for sex appeal is a crossword convention worth learning; 'Victor' is not a name but the radio code word for V.
explanation.definitionFit: To savage something is to attack it ferociously, whether physically like a dog or verbally like a critic.

clue.text: Demonstrate king, for one, is especially fine specimen

blocks.note: to demonstrate is to show
the king is one of the pieces in chess

explanation.surface: Showing off a king as a fine specimen, like a prize exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' signals that the king is an example of a class, here the chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an item displayed because it is an outstanding example of its kind.

clue.text: Dell remodel a vaunted revolutionary part

indicators.note: a part is only a portion of the whole, so the letters come from a stretch of the words
a revolution turns something round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word, the lone letter and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A computer maker's much-hyped remodelled machine has a radical new component.
explanation.walkthrough: Dell looks like the computer company, but it is an ordinary word for a small valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dell is a small wooded hollow, and a vale is a valley, so the two are close synonyms in poetic landscape vocabulary.

clue.text: Huge performance trick

blocks.note: a gig is a live musical performance
an antic is a prank or silly trick

explanation.surface: A stage show featuring an enormous magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: An antic, usually met in the plural, is a playful or foolish stunt; add it to a short word for a concert booking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size, far larger than ordinary.

clue.text: Set off from meeting around school

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it, so the outer piece wraps the inner

blocks.note: a date is an arranged meeting
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a gathering held near a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads like departing from a meeting, but it means making something explode. Eton is the default school in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or firework is to make it explode, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Four surrounded by drink still going strong

indicators.note: something surrounded by another thing is enclosed within it

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four friends round the beer are still drinking vigorously late into the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers in clues often become Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still going strong continues to live and function actively, a figurative sense of being living.

clue.text: Show bum whitish illegal booze

blocks.note: to moon is to bare your backside as a prank
a light colour is pale, close to white

explanation.surface: A rowdy drinker drops their trousers after too much pale bootleg liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is British slang for the backside. The setter uses the answer as a variant of moonshine, spirits distilled illegally, a rare sense most solvers will know only as moonshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled spirits are known as moonshine, and the setter treats this rarer variant of that word as meaning smuggled or bootleg liquor.

clue.text: Chop drugs up with love to produce lozenges

indicators.note: cut or broken up means reduced to bits, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Chopping up medication with care to make throat sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' looks like the instruction, but it is part of the letters to rearrange; 'up' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lozenges are medicated sweets sucked to soothe a sore throat, which is exactly what these are.

clue.text: Privy to put hole in pub

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to insert it, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
O is round like a hole

explanation.surface: Someone is told to punch a hole in the pub, as a toilet joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privy' looks like the old word for an outside toilet, but with 'to' it means sharing in a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To be privy to a secret is to be in on it, meaning included among those who know.

clue.text: Puts an end to including heads of grilled grouse in bar snacks

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
to include something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: to scotch a rumour or plan is to put an end to it
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A pub stops serving snacks that contain grilled grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The two initials slip in just before the final S. A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: These breaded, sausage-wrapped eggs are a classic cold snack served in British pubs alongside drinks.

clue.text: Featureless second print scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull second printing of a book was thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapped' reads as discarding the print run, but it tells you to break the two words up and rebuild them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something featureless lacks any distinctive qualities, which is what this word for dull and unremarkable describes.

clue.text: Desperation born as feasts end in chaos

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: née marks a woman's name at birth
to feast is to dine
the final letter

explanation.surface: Desperate hunger shows as banquets break down in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Née, French for born, is a crossword favourite for these three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperation is a state of great want, and neediness is the condition of lacking and craving things.

clue.text: Quiet craftsperson is biased

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
an artisan is a skilled craftsperson

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken craftsman shows prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quiet comes from musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan view strongly favours one side or party, which makes it prejudiced rather than neutral.

clue.text: Caught bumpkin getting physical exercise with a plant

blocks.note: c is caught in cricket scoring
a hick is an unsophisticated country person
PE is physical education, school exercise
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country yokel is caught doing a workout alongside a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a leguminous crop grown for its edible seeds, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Greeting first lady and chaps during do for success

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within it, so pieces go inside

blocks.note: to do something is to act
hi is a greeting
in the Bible Eve was the first woman
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Greeting the president's wife and her escorts at a party is a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's spouse, but it is Eve; and 'do' looks like a party but is the verb to act.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement is something accomplished by effort, which is what success in a task amounts to.

clue.text: One gliding right behind fish

indicators.note: what comes behind something follows it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: the skate is a flat fish
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Something glides along just behind a fish in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the letter after the fish, since in a down clue later means lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on ice skates moves smoothly across the surface, so the person is literally one who glides.

clue.text: Takes in commercial and chooses

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement or commercial
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone watches an advert and makes a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes in' looks like watching or absorbing the advert, but it means giving a home to a child or pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in a child or animal as your own is to give it a permanent home legally or informally.

clue.text: Heads of the assembly cautiously try diplomacy

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: The leaders of a parliament carefully attempt diplomatic negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of the assembly' suggests parliamentary leaders, but it means the first letter of each following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy in everyday dealings means handling people sensitively, which is the skill this word names.

clue.text: Got free ride from two jerks and Duke

blocks.note: a hitch is a sharp pull, and a hike is a sudden upward yank, so both are jerks
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A nobleman cadges a lift from two idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like fools, but it means sudden tugs, and two different words for a tug are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by thumbing lifts from passing drivers means getting transport without paying for it.

clue.text: Army brag derisively at first

indicators.note: what comes at first in a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to crow is to boast
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers boast mockingly about an early victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' looks like soldiers but is used loosely, as in an army of fans.
explanation.definitionFit: An army can mean any large number of people gathered together, which is what a throng or multitude is.

clue.text: Frank is force-fed regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is routinely force-fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank speech is open and unrestrained, the sense of being unconstrained in what you say.

clue.text: Woman’s embraced by awful poseur – one with special powers

indicators.note: something awful is badly made, so these letters are reordered
to be embraced is to be held within another's arms

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is hugged by a dreadful show-off who claims magical abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split, with the possessive word slotted in before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic-book hero has abilities beyond ordinary humans, such as flight or great strength.

clue.text: Apply for example to return outfit

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to apply paint is to put it on
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Someone applies to send back an unwanted set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apply' reads like making an application, but it means putting something on.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an informal word for a costume or set of clothes, often an eye-catching one.

clue.text: Tidies leaderless canteens in disarray

indicators.note: without a leader means the front letter is dropped
things in disarray are jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone cleans up messy canteens that have lost their manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' suggests canteens without a boss, but it removes the first letter before the rest is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy a room is to put it in order and make it neat, the same action as this verb.

clue.text: Wishes knight in river success at first

indicators.note: a thing in another sits inside it
what comes at first in a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a knight is addressed as Sir
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A knight wading in a river hopes for early success.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee flows through Wales, England and Scotland and is a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishes and desires are both things a person longs for or wants to happen.
